readme_head:
# SafeSweep **Race Jev across two minesweeper boards from the same opening square, where every reveal is a bet that the square is safe.** ![Play: safesweep.jevplay.games](https://img.shields.io/badge/Play-safesweep.jevplay.games-F386A1?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) ![Status: live](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-live-E551BA?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) ![Node: 22.16+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node-22.16%2B-F386A1?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) ![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-DEDEDE?style=flat-square&labelColor=1E1E1E) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Analytics](#analytics) · [Enable Jev](#enable-jev) · [Discord and rankings](#discord-and-rankings) · [Tests, replay verification and benchmarks](#tests-replay-verification-and-benchmarks) · [Repository layout](#repository-layout) · [Contributing](#contributing)
--- SafeSweep is a server-authoritative two-board minesweeper race against Jev. Both players open the same coordinate on independently generated boards, and the first to reveal every safe cell wins. Every match produces a deterministic, hash-linked replay, a verified leaderboard entry when it qualifies, and detailed replay-derived analytics. It is part of [jevplay.games](https://jevplay.games) and was called Minesweeper before the rename. > [!NOTE] > **What is shipped and measured.** The game is implemented and locally tested. It is served today at the pre-rename address `minesweeper.jevplay.games`; `safesweep.jevplay.games` (Cloudflare Workers Free plan + D1) goes live at the rename cutover, after which the old address redirects to it (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`). Real TypeSafe credentials, Discord authorization and the Cloudflare deployment itself were not exercised in this environment. Without credentials the game plays against an explicitly labeled local solver, and those games are unofficial. The bundled benchmark contains local baselines only (zero live Jev calls). See [Operational boundaries](#operational-boundaries). ## Quick start Use Node.js **22.16.0 or later** (built-in SQLite; Node prints an experimental warning). There are **no npm runtime dependencies and no frontend build step**. ```sh cd jev-safesweep # the clone directory (jev-minesweeper before the repo rename) npm start ``` Open `http://localhost:3000`. Select **New game**, then click your starting square. The same coordinate opens on the opponent's independently generated board: Jev when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set, otherwise the labeled local heuristic. `npm start` is a local development shim over the same Worker code production runs (`server/worker.js`), with SQLite standing in for D1. It tolerates a missing `.env` and creates a private SQLite database at `data/safesweep.sqlite` (an existing pre-rename `data/minesweeper.sqlite` is reused). To deploy, follow `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (`npm run deploy`, `npm run db:remote`). For configuration, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, edit the relevant values, and restart. On Windows PowerShell, use `Copy-Item .env.example .env`; on macOS/Linux, use `cp .env.example .env`. [START-HERE.md](START-HERE.md) is the same in three steps. ### The game The browser offers beginner (9×9/10), intermediate (16×16/40), and expert (30×16/99) boards. Easy, Normal, Hard, and Jev reasoning levels change deduction and enumeration budgets rather than introducing deliberate random mistakes. Both boards use the same preset but independent hidden layouts. The protected first opening, reveal, flag/unflag, zero expansion, and safe/unsafe chording are implemented.
